app.name: CaseStudy Hub
app.fullName: AI-Powered Case Study Presentation & Assessment Platform
app.tagline: Run the whole case study cycle in one place: assign, analyse, present, question, assess.

landing.heroTitle: Case study teaching, from assignment to assessment
landing.heroSubtitle: A bilingual platform for universities: class and group management, a case study library, live presentations with class questions, peer review, AI-assisted evaluation and lecturer-approved grading.
landing.heroNote: Phase 1 is under construction. This page is the first deployable slice.
landing.pillar1Body: Cases, guides, groups, schedules, submissions and results of many courses, classes and semesters in one system.
landing.pillar2Body: The class asks, challenges, votes and reviews from their phones while a group presents.
landing.pillar3Body: AI analysis, peer review and the lecturer's decision, each kept as evidence of how a student developed.
landing.frameworkTitle: The presentation framework the platform ships with
landing.frameworkSubtitle: E-Commerce 2026 — Standard Case Study Presentation Framework. Every value below is configuration, not code, so another course can change it.
landing.rolesSubtitle: Context → Mechanism → Numbers → Critique → Transfer → Decision. Every member owns one link of the chain and answers questions on it.
landing.rubricSubtitle: AI may draft the first five criteria against the case, the guide and the submission. Delivery and coordination stays with the lecturer.
landing.phase1Body: Accounts, roles, classes, groups, role allocation, case library, assignments and submissions.
landing.phase2Body: Live presentation room, timer, question wall, Q&A by role and peer assessment.
landing.phase3Body: Document processing, rubric evaluation with citations, question generator and the grading engine.
landing.phase4Body: CLO analytics, learning portfolio, contribution tracker and LMS integration.

framework.title: Assessment framework
framework.subtitle: The rules every mark is computed from: how long a group speaks, how many questions the class owes, what each criterion is worth. Changing a rule publishes a new version. Classes keep the version they were created under, so nothing already marked can move.
framework.versionsBody: A version is never edited. This list only grows, which is what makes an old mark reproducible.
framework.summary: {minutes} minutes · {questions} questions from the class · {team}% group weighting
framework.frameworkIdHint: Keep the name to add a version other classes will inherit; change it to start a separate framework.
framework.frameworkIdHintLecturer: Change this to a new name: adding a version to a framework other classes already use is an administrator's decision.
framework.newVersionHint: Any text, as long as it has not been used for this framework before.
framework.hardStopHint: The clock turns red here. It cannot be earlier than the longest presentation.
framework.teamWeightHint: The individual share is the rest, so the two always add to a whole.
framework.rubricBody: The wording of each criterion is carried over unchanged. The version on screen totals {total} points; the total of the new version follows whatever you put here.
framework.reasonBody: A framework change outlives whoever made it. This is written to the audit log with the new version.
framework.published: The new version is published. Classes created from now on will use it; existing classes keep theirs.
framework.cloBody: What the faculty calls each outcome, and which criteria measure it. The mapping is carried with the framework, so a report keeps the mapping it was produced under.
framework.cloThresholdHint: The share of an outcome's points a piece of work must reach. This is a faculty decision, not a default.
framework.cloConfirmedHint: Until this is ticked, every report says on its face that the mapping is illustrative.

systemAdmin.registrationOpenHint: Close this once a term has started, and add late arrivals from the user page.
systemAdmin.maxImportKbHint: A faculty list is a few kilobytes. Anything much larger is not a class list.
systemAdmin.aiMonthlyCallBudgetHint: Zero stops the AI features without unsetting the credentials.
systemAdmin.reasonHint: Recorded with the change, for whoever reads the log later.
systemAdmin.saved: Saved. These apply from now, to everybody.
systemAdmin.aiStatusBody: Every AI feature here is advisory, so "not configured" is something the interface reports rather than an error. That makes a genuine failure — a wrong model name, a service account without the role — look exactly the same from the outside. This is where the two are told apart.
systemAdmin.aiOffHint: Nothing on this deployment would answer. For Gemini over Vertex AI, run scripts/enable-ai.sh and use the switch below; for OpenAI, or a Gemini API key, enter the key under "Model provider" above. The platform works without a model either way.
systemAdmin.aiProbeCost: Asks the model one trivial question, through the same gateway every other call uses. It counts as one call against the month's budget.
systemAdmin.aiProbeNotConfigured: No model is configured for this deployment, so nothing was called.
systemAdmin.aiProbeBudget: The month's budget of {budget} calls is spent, so nothing was called.
systemAdmin.aiProbeFailed: The model was called and the call failed. The reply is below, exactly as it came back.
systemAdmin.aiToggleHint: Takes effect at once, for everybody. Vertex AI needs no secret — only this switch — so no deploy can change it and no deploy can undo it.
systemAdmin.aiProviderBody: Whose model the platform calls, and with which key. One provider for the whole platform rather than one per class: two classes marked by two different models are two different standards.
systemAdmin.aiProviderHint: Changing this takes effect at once, for every AI feature.
systemAdmin.aiModelHint: Must match a name in that provider's catalogue. Each provider keeps its own, so switching back and forth loses neither.
systemAdmin.aiTransportHint: Vertex AI uses the Cloud Run service account and needs no secret at all. The API key route needs one and is quicker to try.
systemAdmin.aiLocationHint: global serves everywhere and is the least region-restricted.
systemAdmin.aiKeyStored: A key is stored (…{hint}). Leave empty to keep it.
systemAdmin.aiKeyMissing: No key stored. Without one the model will not answer.
systemAdmin.aiProviderSaved: Saved. Use "Ask the model" below to be sure it really answers.

caseSelection.title: Choose your group's case study
caseSelection.body: First come, first served: once a group takes a case, no other group in this class can. Cases another group has taken stay on the list so you can see where they went.
caseSelection.alreadyChosen: Your group has chosen. Ask your lecturer if you need to change it.
caseSelection.cannotChoose: You can see what is left, but choosing is done by a group — and only while the window is open.
caseSelection.boardBody: Either you assign each group a case, or the groups take one each. A group can only take a case no other group in this class holds.
caseSelection.releasePrompt: Why is the claim on {case} being released?
caseSelection.schedulingNote: Choosing a case does not schedule the presentation. Set the date yourself under Assignments — you own the timetable, and a released case cannot be taken back once work exists under it.

dossier.title: Presentation dossier
dossier.openFromMarking: Open the full dossier: every question and every peer score
dossier.neverPresented: this group has not presented yet
dossier.questionsCount: {total} questions, {answered} answered aloud. The framework asks for at least {min} from the class.
dossier.noQuestions: The class asked nothing. That is worth knowing too.
dossier.upvotes: {count, plural, =0 {no upvotes} one {# upvote} other {# upvotes}}
dossier.scoresEvidence: Peer scores are evidence for your judgement. They are never added to a mark.
dossier.scoresCount: {count} of {eligible} students who could score did.

project.title: Class group project
project.lecturerHint: One project for the whole class, with one deadline for every group — separate from the case studies set during the term. In practice the deadline falls in the final week.
project.studentHint: The class group project, due at the deadline below. This is separate work from the case study your group is preparing to present.
project.subject: Class group project
project.deadlineHint: One deadline for the whole class. Anything handed in after it is marked late, by the server clock.
project.reasonHint: At least 10 characters. Recorded with who made the change.
project.scheduled: Project deadline set. Groups can see it on the class page at once.
project.notSetYet: No deadline set yet, so the project is not visible to students.
project.noGroups: This class has no groups to hand work in.
